findings.note: Glossary drift: 'check-in' is now spelled चेक-इन here and in action_named, while the shipped corpus spells the same English concept with the verb हालचाल (ui.notices.aida.paused_receipt, ui.notices.aida.resumed_receipt) and elides it entirely in ui.chat.run_details.wake.managed_note. Both spellings named: चेक-इन (noun, this file, 2 occurrences corpus-wide, both in this namespace) vs हालचाल (verb, 2 occurrences, ui.notices.aida.* only). The loan is defensible — the corpus carries the same X-इन pattern (साइन-इन, 47 occurrences across 16 files) and हालचाल पूछना cannot become a cancellable noun — so nothing is wrong on screen; the cost is one concept in two words across the product. Remedy belongs to the two ui.notices.aida.* keys when next touched, not to this file.

'… इसे दोबारा नहीं बनाया जाएगा' renders 'nothing re-creates it' as an agentless passive, so the reassurance reads 'it will not be created again' and drops the explicit nobody-re-arms-it. The reader-facing fact survives and the passive keeps the card short; the literal alternative would be '… और इसे दोबारा कोई नहीं बनाएगा।'. Recorded, no action required.

English distinguishes 'cadence' from 'schedule'; hi uses शेड्यूल for both ('{name} का अपना शेड्यूल प्रभावित नहीं होगा।' for 'cadence'). I judge this the correct merge, not a defect: the shipped sibling ui.chat.run_details.wake.managed_note already says '{name} का अपना शेड्यूल', so the two sentences agree, and कैडेंस exists nowhere in the corpus. Recorded so a future glossary pass can state that hi merges cadence into शेड्यूल.

Width: 'जागृति रद्द करें' is 16 chars against 'Cancel wake' 11 (1.45x; the only string above 1.30x in the namespace). It shares a justify-end row with Keep (रहने दें) in a 288px card with p-4 padding, leaving ~256px of content box; by char estimate the pair needs ~220-235px, so it should fit but with thin headroom and no wrap guard. Recommend one rendered check of the button row at hi rather than an assertion of overflow — I did not render it.

binding: Verified before writing, not assumed: all five declared sha256 read FIRST and all matched (landed hi, en source, en sidecar, audited draft); the landed file is byte-identical to the audited draft (cmp, plus each hashes to 19c0bcc1) and is the tracked blob at 90f0f49 (git cat-file HEAD:... re-hashes to 19c0bcc1). 12 keys in both locales, set-difference empty both ways, order equal to English, sidecar keys == English keys, 12 distinct hi values, none byte-identical to English. Parsed both sides with the repo's own @formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser: argument names and select arms identical per key (5 simple placeholders per side, select(subject) arms head/other on both message keys, no plural/date/number skeleton anywhere in the namespace, so no locale plural-category question arises). Rendered both message keys with IntlMessageFormat from the repo's node_modules at subject=head and subject=other with Atlas, Research agent and a quoted head: both arms select correctly and agree in gender (नहीं जगेगी with जागृति, {name} का with the possessed masculine चेक-इन/शेड्यूल, so a feminine assistant name is safe). Format: TAB indent (12 tab lines, 0 space lines), exactly one trailing newline, no BOM, no CR, no \u escapes, NFC clean, no bidi/format characters (hi is LTR; the ur RTL clause does not apply here). English sweep: zero Latin runs in any value outside ICU syntax; the only Latin is the structural words subject/select/head/other/name inside the ICU braces plus the {name}/{head} tokens — no English fragment ships. Loader wiring: hiUiChatRunControls is imported at src/i18n/keys.gen.ts:585 and spread into the hi map at :1920, so the namespace resolves from this file with no English fallback. Judged all 12 values myself against English and the sidecar; carried the earlier MINOR and two NITs only where I independently agree they stand, and added one new NIT (button width).
